subject: Hosted evaluation: activation plan & rate thresholds
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@finlytics.io>, Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 May 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation: activation plan & rate thresholds

Hi Alice, Samir —

Great to meet you both on the demo earlier. Quick recap and a concrete activation proposal so we can move from demo -> sandbox pilot for Hosted: 

Summary of what you said on the call:
- Preference: start with Hosted API (fastest path to productizing the convo assistant)
- Expected steady-state: ~50 RPS initially, seasonal spikes up to ~150 RPS
- Typical request: ~1.2k tokens in prompt + up to 800 tokens for generation (avg ~2k tokens per request)
- Data residency: US-only for now; potential EU rollouts later

Proposed quickstart (what Redwood will deliver):
1) Sandbox access + one dedicated sandbox endpoint for your team (prefix: /v1/finlytics-sandbox)
2) Activation checklist and ops preflight (network allowlist, API keys, rate-slice proposal) — attached: redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf
3) Pilot rate-slice: start with a 50 RPS per-key pilot slice with burst up to 150 RPS for 10m windows while we observe latency and token cost.
4) Ops call week-of Mon/Tue next week to validate network egress and SSO onboarding.

Questions for you (action items):
- Please confirm the expected peak QPS and largest token size we should plan for (you mentioned ~2k tokens).
- Share a representative traffic sample (CSV) and any IP allowlist requirements — I’ve attached a network-ips.csv template you can fill.
- Confirm whether you need per-route caps or per-key caps (we can configure both).

Next steps I’ll take from our side:
- Create sandbox endpoint and pre-seed keys by EOD tomorrow.
- Share a short Ops preflight agenda for the call.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf, network-egress-ips.csv

Thanks — looking forward to getting you into a sandbox and measuring real traffic.

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
pri@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0123

From: Alice Chen <alice@finlytics.io>
To: Priyom Das <pri@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.io>
Date: Sat, 10 May 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: activation plan & rate thresholds

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifying items from our side before the ops call: 

- Rate expectations: the 50 RPS steady state is correct to start; we expect three 10‑minute bursts per day that could push ~120–150 RPS.
- Token sizes: worst case ~2.5k tokens for some long-context customer sessions; average ~1.8–2.0k.
- Residency: must remain US-only for the pilot.
- Are prefix/KV cache hints available on Hosted to improve cost for repeated context?
- What are typical latency percentiles for that token size on Hosted endpoints? SLA targets we should plan for?
- Billing model: are pilot tokens billed at list hosted rate or is there a trial credit structure?

We can provide a traffic sample (CSV) — attaching a quick export. Also, Samir will be on the ops call (he’s cc’d).

Thanks — available for the call Thursday morning PST.

—
Alice Chen
Head of Product, FinLytics
alice@finlytics.io

On Fri, May 9, 2025 at 3:12 PM Priyom Das <pri@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Great to meet you both on the demo earlier. Quick recap and a concrete activation proposal so we can move from demo -> sandbox pilot for Hosted: ...

From: Priyom Das <pri@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@finlytics.io>, Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 May 2025 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: activation plan & rate thresholds

Hi Alice, Samir —

Appreciate the details — helpful. Short answers and an updated action list below.

1) Prefix / KV cache: yes — Hosted supports prefix-aware KV caching and configurable TTLs. For repeated conversational snippets we typically see 30–60% token savings depending on prompt variance; we’ll enable a conservative TTL for the pilot.

2) Latency: for ~2k token end-to-end generative completions on our Hosted pilot fleet we typically hit P50 ~210ms for decoding-only paths and P95 ~450–700ms depending on model and concurrency. We’ll instrument percentiles on your sandbox endpoint and share a live dashboard.

3) Billing for pilot: we can apply pilot credits for the first 30 days — we’ll bill at hosted list rates and then apply the credit to offset. If you prefer, we can define a limited trial quote instead (I’ll loop finance if needed).

Updated activation plan (what I’ll provision by EOD):
- Sandbox endpoint: /v1/finlytics-sandbox (API key scoped to your team)
- Pilot rate-slice: 50 RPS steady, burst up to 150 RPS windows (configurable)
- Ops preflight agenda: network allowlist, SSO, test vectors, alerting hooks

Action items for FinLytics (Alice/Samir):
- Send the traffic sample CSV to me (I see you attached one — thanks)
- Confirm any specific IP ranges or private peering needs (if you require private VPC later we’ll capture details now)
- Confirm Thursday 10:30am PST for the ops preflight call — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: finlytics-traffic-sample.csv (from Alice)

Cc’ing Marissa and Ben to help with sandbox provisioning and billing touchpoints. Marissa — can you take the provisioning action and create the sandbox endpoint once I confirm the key scope? Ben — can you note the billing/credit option so we can present a short pilot quote if the customer wants it.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the invite.

—
Priyom

From: Alice Chen <alice@finlytics.io>

Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.io>

Thanks Priyom — that all sounds good.

We confirm:
- Thursday 10:30am PST works for the preflight call.
- We’ll share the fuller traffic export and our IP ranges by EOD Monday.
- For the pilot we’ll proceed on Hosted. If we see sustained >400 RPS needs within 60 days we may discuss Dedicated.

I’ve attached the traffic export for now. Looking forward to the invite.

Attachments: finlytics-traffic-sample.csv

—
Alice
